clue.text: Old lovers view sex differently

indicators.note: doing something differently means arranging it another way, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Former partners have changed their attitude to sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex-wives are women someone was once married to, so former partners in love.

clue.text: Forceful politician, hard one to quote without getting upset

indicators.note: without here means outside, so this piece wraps the others
upset means turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses the word

parts.note: to cite is to quote
a means one
H for hard, as on pencils
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A strident politician who is impossible to quote without losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means expressed with force and insistence, hence forceful.

clue.text: Devious wiretap traps Panama's top ecstasy/marijuana transporter

indicators.note: something devious takes a winding, indirect route, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word is its head, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Panama
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sneaky phone tap catches a Panamanian drug lord moving pills and cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of wiretap plus the two trapped letters: the blog reading is wiretap rearranged with P and E caught inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe, or bong, is a device through which cannabis smoke is drawn through water.

clue.text: Precise guards provided evidence

indicators.note: guards stand around what they protect, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: very can mean precise, as in the very thing
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Exact security staff gave proof in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evidence' is the verb here, to show or prove something.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify a claim is to confirm it, which is what evidencing it does.

clue.text: American brought up his poorly prepared food

indicators.note: brought up means raised, which in a down entry reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: US for American

indicators.note: something badly made up is put together wrongly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American vomited his badly cooked dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests vomiting, but it is raising a word in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice, often with raw fish, a kind of food.

clue.text: It's Spooner's dad who's reserved takeaway?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase is to be said his way

parts.note: a reserved dad is a shy pop; swapping the opening sounds gives the phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a famously tongue-tied clergyman would call his bashful father.
explanation.walkthrough: SHY POP becomes PIE SHOP when the sh and p sounds trade places. The question mark flags that a pie shop is only one example of a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie shop sells food to carry out and eat elsewhere, an example of a takeaway outlet.

clue.text: Heroin supplier went soft inside, letting head drop

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into the other
the head drops to the bottom, so the first letter moves to the end of the word

parts.note: peed means urinated, went to the toilet
soppy means soft and sentimental

explanation.surface: A drug dealer became a softie, hanging his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the colloquial sense of going to the lavatory, and 'Heroin supplier' is fair because heroin is refined from the opium poppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium poppies grow from seeds, and heroin is refined from opium, so the seed is the source.

clue.text: Greatness can emerge from Harpenden (or MIT/Yale)

indicators.note: something that emerges from within was inside all along, so the letters are concealed in the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of Harpenden, or, MIT and the start of Yale

explanation.surface: Great minds can come from a Hertfordshire town as readily as from elite universities.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpenden is a commuter town in Hertfordshire, north of London. Enormity is used here in its contested sense of hugeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormity is often used to mean great size or scale, a synonym of greatness.

clue.text: Rob Holding expects Ipswich to start with speediest wingers

indicators.note: to start means taking only the beginnings, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the two outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of speediest

explanation.surface: An Arsenal defender anticipates a match where Ipswich begin with their quickest wide men.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Holding is an English footballer, which disguises 'Rob' as a name; it is the definition, a verb used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, and in informal English a rob can mean a robbery.

clue.text: Sanctimonious German writer's filthy accommodation

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
G for German
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A self-righteous German author lives in squalid lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigpen is a sty, and the word is used for any very dirty place to live.

clue.text: Sellers gaze across the far side of market

indicators.note: to stretch across something is to span it, so one piece goes on either side of the other

parts.note: to peer is to gaze closely

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of market

explanation.surface: Traders at a stall look over to the far end of the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like market traders, but it is the comic actor Peter Sellers, defined by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Sellers was the English comic actor of the Pink Panther films, so Sellers is a person called Peter.

clue.text: How about drink before setting?

indicators.note: coming before something means placed ahead of it, so the pieces are joined in the order given

parts.note: to sup is to drink
setting a question is posing it

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a drink before the sun sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' suggests sunset, but here it is setting in the sense of putting forward, as with a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposing, like 'how about', introduces a hypothetical suggestion: supposing we went out?

clue.text: Insubstantial brownies? First piece dispatched

indicators.note: dispatching the first piece sends away the opening letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a brownie is a household sprite, a kind of fairy; the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A question about whether chocolate brownies are too light, with the first slice already gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brownies' suggests cake, but it means the helpful household sprites of folklore. Two fairies make the plural, then the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes ideas that are vague and lacking any solid substance.

clue.text: Rhythmic use of words shows man in Paris to be French

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French man
être is the French verb meaning to be

explanation.surface: Poetry shows that a Parisian man is truly French.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the regular pattern of stressed syllables in verse, its rhythmic arrangement.

clue.text: Retiring personal assistant gets colourful ring

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is taken backwards

parts.note: Siri is Apple's voice-controlled personal assistant

explanation.surface: A shy secretary is given a bright ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring personal assistant' reads as a shy secretary, but the assistant is the software on an iPhone.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the pigmented ring around the pupil that gives the eye its colour.

clue.text: Vote Little Richard 'exhilarating'

parts.note: to elect is to vote in
Ric is a short form of Richard

explanation.surface: A fan's poll endorsement calling the rock and roll singer Little Richard thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard looks like the singer, but 'Little' just asks for a shortened Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric atmosphere or performance is thrilling, charged with excitement.

clue.text: Former politician maybe reading first books: he likes the ones with stickers!

definitions.text: he likes the ones with stickers

parts.note: an ex-Lib is a former Liberal
R for reading, one of the three Rs
1st written out with I for the numeral

explanation.surface: A retired politician enjoys books with stickers in them.
explanation.walkthrough: The stickers are bookplates, the labels pasted inside a cover reading ex libris, 'from the library of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-librist is a collector of bookplates, the ownership labels stuck in books.

clue.text: Inept old minister initially shaken, church members not being up for service

definitions.text: members not being up for service

indicators.note: shaken things are tossed about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O for old

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter of minister
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A doddering clergyman is shaken while his congregation won't turn up to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' and 'service' look churchy, but the definition is a bawdy one about men unable to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotence is the inability to achieve an erection, here jokingly a member not up for duty.

clue.text: Bent cop's car carries heroin, a reliable money-maker

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so a letter is placed inside
bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the words as written
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A corrupt officer's car is smuggling heroin, a steady earner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash crop is grown to sell for profit rather than for the farmer's own use.

clue.text: Wheels are so versatile

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wheels are entirely circular
second meaning: good at many things

explanation.surface: A claim that wheels are adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally as completely round.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-round player is skilled in every aspect, which is what versatile means.

clue.text: Comprehensive contract covers termination

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps around it, so one piece sits outside the other

parts.note: a deed is a legal contract
the tail is the end or termination of something

explanation.surface: A full contract includes a clause about ending it.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed account is thorough and comprehensive, covering every particular.

clue.text: Stone wall's bare, needing work on face

indicators.note: placed on the face means at the front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: stripped bare means the outer layer is taken off, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the middle letters of wall

explanation.surface: A stone wall is unrendered and needs work doing to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone, so it is a stone in the jeweller's sense.

clue.text: Shade diminishing as wife moves south

indicators.note: south is downward, which in a down entry shifts a letter one place lower

parts.note: waning means shrinking or diminishing
W for wife

explanation.surface: The light is fading as a wife heads south.
explanation.walkthrough: WANING turns into the answer when its W slips down one place below the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canopy that gives shade over a window or shopfront.

clue.text: Mapmakers following city descent

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapping agency

explanation.surface: Cartographers come after a city's decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an anticlimactic drop from the elevated to the trivial, a descent in tone.

clue.text: Why, for the most part, entertaining fellas regularly fail to pay

indicators.note: for the most part means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: why without its last letter

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of fellas

explanation.surface: Asking why the blokes who are regularly hosted never settle up.
explanation.walkthrough: To welsh on a debt is to dodge paying it; some consider the term offensive to the Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh is to break an agreement by avoiding payment of what one owes.

clue.text: Put a brake on Coot's drunken arrests

indicators.note: arresting someone means holding them, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
the setter Coot speaking of himself: I'm

explanation.surface: The setter's drunken behaviour is checked.
explanation.walkthrough: Coot is the setter, so 'Coot's' means the setter is, I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict it, to put a brake on it.

clue.text: Slander cricketer possessing unnatural ability?

indicators.note: something possessing another holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a batter is a cricketer at the crease
ESP, extrasensory perception, is a supposed supernatural faculty

explanation.surface: Accusing a cricketer of having uncanny powers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespatter someone figuratively is to throw mud at their reputation, to defame them.

clue.text: Fibrous tissue is held up, previously unseen

indicators.note: held up means raised, so in a down entry the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
something new has not been seen before

explanation.surface: A sample of fibrous tissue is held up to reveal something never seen before.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, a tough band of fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Perhaps baptism's slammed in memoirs

indicators.note: something slammed is knocked about violently, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A christening is criticised harshly in someone's autobiography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks baptism as an example: some churches baptise by full immersion in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Immersion, dipping a person fully under water, is one form that baptism takes.

clue.text: One who follows march in dull clothes

indicators.note: clothes cover what is inside them, so the letters sit concealed within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of march, all of in and the start of dull

explanation.surface: Someone marching behind others while dressed in drab outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who follows' is fair because a Hindu is a follower of the religion of Hinduism.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is an adherent of Hinduism, so a follower of a faith.

clue.text: Decline brought surgical procedure and occupational therapy

parts.note: got can mean brought, as in got the car round
op is short for operation
OT is the standard abbreviation for occupational therapy

explanation.surface: A patient's decline led to an operation followed by rehabilitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating through neglect.

clue.text: Time for Biden to wander around shopping centre?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to wend is to make one's way
Eastern Standard Time, the zone of Washington DC where Biden worked

explanation.surface: The president is due an afternoon browsing a shopping mall.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is central London's main shopping and theatre district; the question mark admits it is more than a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: London's West End is home to Oxford Street and Regent Street, a famous centre for retail.
